faq: Which databases do you work with?
PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB and Redis, on managed services such as Amazon RDS, Google Cloud SQL and Azure, or on your own server. Tell us what you use and we confirm fit.
Will you see my customer data?
We set up access and structure, and we do not need to browse customer records. Where we must look at data to tune a query, we ask for a copy with personal details removed.
Can you move my database to a new host?
Yes, in the Premium package. We copy the data, check row counts, test your app against the new one and plan a short switch-over window. A rehearsal is run first.
What does a restore test involve?
We restore a recent backup to a separate copy, check that the data is complete and time how long it takes. You get the result in writing, so you know the backups work.

desc:
Database setup, security and backups give your app a safe place to keep its data. Ecom Swift LLC creates or tidies your PostgreSQL, MySQL or MongoDB database, locks down access, turns on encryption and schedules backups you can restore from.

## What does a secure database setup involve?

A secure database setup means the right engine, the right users and a private path to reach it. The database is not open to the public internet. Each user can do only what its job needs. Data is encrypted while stored and while moving. Copies are taken on a schedule and tested.

Many databases start life in a hurry. A developer creates one with an admin login, opens access to every address so the app can connect and promises to tighten it later. Later rarely comes, and that open door is exactly what automated scanners look for.

## Why database mistakes cost so much

The database holds your customers, orders, content and history. A weak setup puts all of it at risk at once. An exposed port can lead to stolen records. A shared admin login means one leaked password reaches everything. A missing backup turns a mistyped command into permanent loss.

Performance problems also begin here. A table without the right index makes a page slow once data grows. Too many open connections can stall an app during a busy hour. These issues are cheaper to prevent in setup than to chase during an incident.

## How good data foundations help your app

A well-configured database makes the whole product steadier. Pages load faster when queries use indexes. The app stays up under load when connections are pooled. Developers ship with more confidence because they have separate users for each environment and a clear process for schema changes.

It also reduces risk for you as the owner. If an employee leaves or a credential leaks, limited permissions contain the damage. If a release goes wrong, a tested backup lets you go back. That is the practical value: fewer emergencies, and shorter ones when they do happen.

## What a well-run database includes

- The right engine for your data, whether relational like PostgreSQL and MySQL or document-based like MongoDB.
- Separate users for the app, for reporting and for administration, each with minimum permissions.
- Public access closed, with connections allowed only from your app or a private network.
- Encryption at rest and in transit.
- Scheduled backups with a retention rule and a restore test.
- Connection pooling so busy periods do not exhaust connections.
- An index and slow-query review for the tables your app reads most.
- Alerts for disk space, memory and failed backups.
- A replica or failover option when downtime is costly.
- Connection notes so developers know how to reach each environment.

## How we do the work

We first look at what exists: engine, version, hosting, users and network rules. If you are starting fresh, we help choose the engine and plan size. Then we create the users, close public access, enable encryption and set backups.

The middle package adds performance work and a real restore test. The Premium package can add a read replica or failover, a data move from an older host, monitoring and a repeatable schema migration process. We do not need to read your customer records to do any of this. Our work is on structure, access and settings, and we ask your developers for help only where the app itself must change.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give each app and person a separate login.
- Keep the database on a private network where possible.
- Test a restore before you rely on a backup.
- Record connection details in a secrets store, not in code.
- Review slow queries when traffic grows.

**Avoid:**
- Using one all-powerful admin login everywhere.
- Opening the database to every address for convenience.
- Skipping updates because the system seems stable.
- Keeping backups only on the database server itself.
- Changing a live schema without a rollback plan.

## Who this is for

This service suits a founder whose developer built the app quickly and left the database wide open. It suits a team moving from a shared host to a managed database service. It also suits an online business that has grown and now sees slow pages at busy times.

## What we need from you

Tell us which database you use or want, where it runs and what app connects to it. We never need your passwords. Access is given as a collaborator, team or limited developer user on your cloud account, and any connection secrets stay in your own secrets store.
